QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_75

question.text: Bharat Asset Management's MF-for-SSE scheme funds an SE that runs BOTH environmental restoration (SAS-500) AND financial inclusion for forest-dwelling communities (SAS-1300). For the aggregate SROI number, the SIA must:

answer.text: Compute standard-specific SROIs with explicit assumption tables (carbon proxy for SAS-500, account-usage proxy for SAS-1300), then report the aggregate with full disclosure — avoiding the temptation to mask assumption heterogeneity by a single weighted-average figure

explanation.text: The Logic: Different SAS standards use different SROI proxies (CO2e monetised for SAS-500; income/insurance value for SAS-1300). Collapsing into one aggregate number without disclosing assumption heterogeneity misleads Report users. Best practice: report each standard's SROI separately with a clearly-disclosed aggregate and assumption annex. The Trap: Option B hides methodological differences. Option C cherry-picks. Option D unjustifiably omits useful info. Cross-Exam Context: Same heterogeneous-assumption disclosure in XV Research Analyst (multi-model valuation) and XIX-A (AIF — NAV across diverse assets). Assessor's Pro-Tip: In the aggregate SROI annex, use a two-column layout: Column 1 = SROI by standard, Column 2 = key assumption summary. One glance gives the reader the full methodological map.
